printed_page_note: no printed page number is legible on this exposure; a continuation sheet's number sits in the top corner the binding takes. Recorded as unknown, not inferred from the ids around it — the sorted filename order is not the book order.
division: S. W. Sherman (as written in the printed heading)
read_pass: the eight middle columns read against the enumerator's own footings: commerce, manufactures and trades and the learned professions CLOSE; mining, agriculture and both navigation columns close at nothing written; the TOTAL column is read on 24 of its 31 numbers and does not close, and its residual is the finding (T-0547)
lines_note: COMMITTED, and demonstrated. The leaf carries 30 line slots at a measured pitch of 75.856 px (line_index.grid, fitted to the industry columns alone, rms 5.8 px) and 29 of them carry a TOTAL number. The thirtieth, k=4 at y974, carries a 15x12 px mark at y958-970 that is real ink but below the instrument's speck filter and is not read as a digit. This supersedes '29 to 31, favouring 31' and the inventory pass's 28.
no_horizontal_rules: MEASURED ON THIS IMAGE: the sheet carries NO horizontal ruled lines inside the body. A row-darkness profile taken across the empty slaves block finds exactly two strong rules on the leaf — the one under the printed heading and the one above the enumerator's footer — and nothing between them: the largest excess over local background anywhere inside the body is 4.0 grey levels, against 77 to 211 for those two printed rules. The printed form rules this page vertically only. That is the reason a continuation sheet is hard to index, and it is the thing the reading of 33S7-9YYJ-5S could not name when it reported that 'nothing on the image settles which [row] without re-reading the sheet against a row grid anchored on the ruled lines': there is no such grid to anchor on. Every row assignment on these three sheets has to come from the enumerator's own ink, and the only column with an entry on every line is TOTAL.
form_note: The right (continuation) sheet of the 1840 schedule. Columns as printed, left to right: twelve SLAVES columns (six male, six female age bands); TOTAL — number of persons in each family; seven NUMBER OF PERSONS IN EACH FAMILY EMPLOYED IN columns (mining, agriculture, commerce, manufactures and trades, navigation of the ocean, navigation of canals lakes and rivers, learned professions and engineers); PENSIONERS FOR REVOLUTIONARY OR MILITARY SERVICES (ages, names); six DEAF AND DUMB, BLIND, AND INSANE WHITE PERSONS columns; four of the same for coloured persons; and seven SCHOOLS, &c. columns. A blank cell on this form is a zero and is recorded as 0.
closure_note: The enumerator added his own totals at the foot of the sheet. Those printed totals are transcribed under `footer_as_read` and are the committed data on this sheet. Where a per-line reading is attempted it is checked against them and its residual recorded; a reading is never adjusted to make a total come out.

footer_as_read.total_note: see footer_total_argument: the arithmetic of the 29 numbers permits 165 and not 105. The claim that the same glyph stands twice in the body is WITHDRAWN — see footer_total_argument.withdrawn.
footer_as_read.footer_blank_columns_note: the mining, agriculture, both navigation, pensioners, deaf/dumb/blind/insane and schools blocks carry no figure at the foot of this sheet

column_ink_census_note: A per-column ink census over the body, counting pixels 70 grey levels below each column's own 60th percentile, is committed under `column_ink_census` as the structural finding it is: it says which columns were written in at all, and it is reproducible from the image without reading a single digit. The single-width columns are clean; the wide blocks (slaves, deaf/dumb/blind/insane, schools) carry many printed rules inside the band and their counts are dominated by those rules, so they are reported but are NOT read as evidence of an entry either way.
records_note: empty on purpose, and for a narrower reason than before. The per-column readings ARE committed — under column_closure, with every entry's y, and under total_column, by glyph group. What is not committed is a row per LINE, because the line INDEX is the open quantity (see lines_note): a record keyed `line: 4` would commit an ordinal the sheet does not carry. The remaining work is that index and the seven unread totals, and it is T-0565.

pairing.why: a continuation sheet carries no name and no printed page number of its own, so the pairing to its left sheet is a separate reading. T-0539 pairs all eleven at once. Recorded as unpaired rather than guessed.
pairing.page_population_key_note: STILL NOT COMMITTED as the key, and deliberately. footer_total_argument makes 165 the only candidate the sheet's own arithmetic permits, but that is an inference resting on three glyph readings, and a wrong key pairs the wrong sheet. T-0539 should try 165 FIRST and treat a failure to pair as evidence against it rather than against the pairing test.
pairing.line_count_key_note: COMMITTED at 30 line slots (29 of them carrying a family) on the grid in line_index. Which of the two a left sheet should be paired on is T-0539's to say; both are stated.

ticket: T-0564 read the columns. T-0565 (this pass) has the line index, the band resolutions and the totals it could read.

column_geometry.note: MEASURED, not assumed. The vertical printed rules are found by CONTINUITY — an x where at least 60 per cent of the body's rows stand darker than their own local background — because a mean-darkness profile of this leaf reports rules at x 1441 and x 1719 that are a family total and a 2. The eight single-width columns are then named off the one run of seven even gaps that is bracketed by a wide cell on both sides: TOTAL on the left, the pensioners AGES column on the right. The right-hand deaf/dumb and schools blocks stand at the same pitch and have no such bracket, which is what tells them apart.

glyph_inventory.note: The tool measures boxes and refuses to name digits, which is the point: a machine guess at a 4 that is two strokes reading as 11 would launder a guess into a measurement. Its group count for the TOTAL column OVER-counts and the sensitivity row above says by how much — the x-does-not-step-back rule splits a number whose parts the hand drew right to left, and this sheet's 5 is drawn top bar first and then the descender. The curated count below, 31 numbers, is the tool's components read by eye at magnification.

total_column.indexed_by: measured image y AND, since this pass, a line ordinal. The ordinal is not assigned: see line_index, where a grid fitted to the industry columns alone — the TOTAL column contributes nothing to the fit — puts all 44 components of this cell inside k=0..29 with none left over. The by_glyph_group entries below keep their y indexing so the two records can be compared group for group.
total_column.residual_note: 21 of the 29 numbers are read and sum to 86. Eight are unread: k=2, k=3, k=5, k=7, k=13, k=27, k=28 and k=29. Against a footing of 165 the residual across those eight is 79 (mean 9.9); against 105 it is 19 (mean 2.4). Neither closes the column, and the column is not stated as closing. What the residual DOES bear on is which footing is possible — see footer_total_argument.
total_column.superseded_group_count: was 31 numbers, 22 read, sum 83. The groups were right; their partition into numbers was not. See line_index: the leaf has 30 line slots at a measured 75.86 px pitch, 29 of them carry a number, and the by_glyph_group list below is 31 GROUPS which are 29 NUMBERS. Two changes of substance: band D (y2699-2772) is one number and not two 1s, which removes 2 from the read sum; and k=25 is READ as 5, which adds 5. 83 - 2 + 5 = 86.

bands_resolved.what_the_ticket_asked: the four bands where consecutive groups stand 32 to 50 px apart against a 58-90 px line pitch, each resolved into one number or two lines, with the evidence stated. T-0565. All four are resolved; two of the four are read. All four are resolved as one-number-or-two-lines; two of the four (C and D) are also read or reduced to one number, and band A's partition is narrowed to two candidates with one favoured.
bands_resolved.pitch_used: 75.856 px, measured (line_index.grid). The 58-90 px range the earlier passes quoted was the spread of observed gaps between adjacent groups, which is not a pitch — it is a pitch seen through missing lines and split glyphs.

band_a.evidence: a one-line reading needs a single number 96 px tall. The tallest number anywhere on this sheet is 54 px (k=26). It would also leave the k=3 slot empty while its own ink straddles it: the ink runs y824-920 and the slot boundary between k=2 and k=3 falls at y860, with #6 wholly above it and #8 wholly below.
band_a.values: NOT READ, but narrowed to one favoured partition. The four strokes are #6 (one stroke of the single-1 form), #7 (one more of the same, 23 px), and #8 (ONE component drawn as two touching strokes — the same form as the confirmed 11s at k=8 and k=23). See band_a_partition.

band_b.verdict: ONE LINE — k=5, therefore ONE number
band_b.evidence: the two groups' centres are 34.5 px apart. The pitch is 75.86 px and the smallest gap between two lines this sheet's own anchors demonstrate is 60 px. No two lines on this leaf can stand 34.5 px apart, so the groups are one number. #9 also sits ABOVE #10 and overlaps it in x, which is stacking, not two digits side by side.

band_c.verdict: ONE LINE — k=25 — and READ as 5
band_c.evidence: independently anchored: the commerce column's 3 stands at y2577, which is k=25 (predicted 2566.7). The two components 32 px apart are the two components of one glyph: #34 is a top bar drawn to the right and #36 is the descender and its bowl, below it and to its LEFT — the identical two-part construction, at the same size and the same relative offset, as the confirmed 5 at k=12 (#20 top bar, #21 descender below-left). That is why the lower component stands further left, which the pass before this one recorded as impossible for the hand: it is not the hand going back for a new number, it is the second stroke of a 5.

band_d.verdict: ONE LINE — k=27 — therefore ONE number, not two
band_d.evidence: the two groups' centres are 50 px apart against the 75.86 px pitch, and the commerce 1 at y2723 anchors k=27 BETWEEN them, so they cannot be two lines. Which line each belongs to is then settled by the anchor-offset test (see anchor_offset_test): against the commerce 1 on this line, #38 alone stands at -3.5 sd, #39 alone at +4.5 sd, and #38 and #39 read as ONE number at +1.0 sd — inside the distribution the other twenty lines draw. The pass before this one read them as two separate 1s; that is withdrawn, and it is what takes the column from 30 numbers to 29.

band_a_partition.state: OPEN, with (ii) favoured. This is the one thing on the sheet the image does not settle: the two tests that settle every other band disagree here, and the disagreement is recorded rather than resolved by preference.
band_a_partition.i: k=2 = {#6}, k=3 = {#7,#8}. Preferred by both position tests: #6 alone is +0.5 sd on the anchor-offset test against the commerce 4 and learned-professions 1 that anchor k=2, and it sits 17 px from the grid line. Cost, and it is a heavy one: it makes k=3 a group of three 1-strokes, and no three-stroke number is read anywhere on this sheet — as a number it would have to be 111.
band_a_partition.ii: k=2 = {#6,#7}, k=3 = {#8}. FAVOURED, because it is the only partition under which both lines are numbers this hand writes: 11 and 11, the first as two separate components like k=1, the second as one two-stroke component like k=8 and k=23. Cost: {#6,#7}'s centre stands +2.8 sd on the anchor-offset test (+23.7 px where the twenty-one anchored lines run -8 to +18), and the two digits are 36 px apart in y where the sheet's other two-glyph numbers show 1 to 16 px.
band_a_partition.not_read_because: one test says (i) and the shape of the hand says (ii). Committing either would be choosing, and the arithmetic below is not evidence for a digit. Recorded as open with the two candidates and the exact cost of each, so the next pass argues from the costs rather than from the question.

total_column.by_glyph_group_note: the 31 GROUPS of the pass before this one, each now carrying the line ordinal the grid assigns it (line = k+1). Two ordinals carry two groups each — k=5 (band B) and k=27 (band D) — because those groups are one number; k=26 also shares y range with band C's third component. The 29 NUMBERS and their values are in line_index.lines, which is the record to read.

anchor_offset_test.what: for each of the 21 lines where an industry column entry and a TOTAL number both stand, the offset between the TOTAL number's y centre and the industry entry's y centre. It needs no grid and no threshold — it is two measured boxes on one line.
anchor_offset_test.result: +6.0 px, sd 6.3, over a range of -8 to +18. The TOTAL number sits a little below its industry anchor, consistently.
anchor_offset_test.why_it_matters: it is an independent arbiter for a band whose line is anchored, and it is what settles band D.

reasoning: THE ARITHMETIC IS STILL ONE-SIDED, AND IT NOW RESTS ON THE COMPONENTS RATHER THAN ON A GLYPH. Twenty-one of the twenty-nine numbers are read unambiguously and sum to 86, leaving eight unread. A footing of 105 leaves 19 across those eight. But four of the eight — k=2, k=3, k=28 and k=29 — are numbers of two glyphs each on the component evidence (line_index names the components and their sizes), and a two-glyph number in this column is at least 10. That is at least 40 into a residual of 19. 105 is unreachable. Under 165 the residual is 79 across the eight, which those four two-glyph numbers and four single ones carry without strain.

THE THREE READINGS THE ARGUMENT RESTS ON ARE NOW CONFIRMED, WHICH CLOSES THE ESCAPE THE LAST PASS NAMED. It recorded that if the 13 at k=0 and the 11s at k=1 and k=23 were instead 3, 4 and 4, the unambiguous sum falls far enough for 105 to be reached. All three were re-read this pass against the sheet's own single 1s at k=14, k=17 and k=21: every stroke of the paired groups is the identical tapered form of those single 1s, and the sheet's 4 — the commerce 4 at y834, which the footer calibrates at 27 — is a closed crossbarred glyph with a descender that shares nothing with a pair of slashes. The 11s are 11 and the 13 is 13.

THE SHEET'S NEIGHBOURS FOOT THE SAME ORDER OF MAGNITUDE. 33S7-9YYJ-24 foots 201 people on 31 lines and another continuation sheet in this group foots 198. 165 over the 29 families this leaf carries is 5.7 per family; 105 would be 3.6, under this deposit's own 1840 mean of 4.6.
footer_total_argument.what_it_rests_on: the count of glyphs in four unread numbers, which is a measurement (8-connected components of the committed image, listed in line_index), and no longer on a reading of the footer's own middle glyph. It is still INFERRED, because 'a two-glyph number is at least 10' is an inference about the hand and not a reading of a digit.
footer_total_argument.supersedes: the pass before this one recorded the middle glyph as unread and would not choose between 0 and 6 "to make a page population". This pass does not choose by looking either. It states what the arithmetic of the read lines permits, and that is one-sided.

withdrawn.claim: the pass before this one argued that the footer total's middle glyph — small, low, a short stroke hooking left at the bottom with a faint return above — is THE SAME GLYPH as the second glyph of the last two numbers in the column, at y2784 and y2860, so that one answer settled all three and the choice was between 105/10/10 and 165/16/16.
withdrawn.why_withdrawn: it does not hold at magnification. The second glyphs at k=28 (#41) and k=29 (#43) are plain tapered slashes of the sheet's single-1 form, drawn without a bowl and without a return. The footer's middle glyph is a bowled form: a stroke that hooks left at the bottom into a closed curve with a faint approach above it. The nearest thing to it on this leaf is the large single glyph at k=13 (#22) — a long horizontal tail at the top right sweeping down-left into a closed bowl — which is also the glyph this pass can say is NOT the sheet's 5, because both confirmed 5s are built as two components and #22 is one.
withdrawn.what_survives: the conclusion, by a different route: see reasoning. The coupling is gone; the arithmetic is stronger than it was, because the sum it works from is now 86 over 21 read numbers on a line index rather than 83 over 22 groups with no index.

The provisional block is removed rather than kept alongside, so there is one reading of each column on this sheet and not two.

line_index.derived_by: the grid below, fitted to the industry columns of this sheet ALONE and then applied to the TOTAL cell; see method. Re-derivable from the committed image with tools/read_census_continuation.py and no number typed in.

grid.fitted_to: the 22 line positions the mining, agriculture, commerce, manufactures-and-trades and learned-professions columns fix by their own entries — the TOTAL column contributes NOTHING to the fit, which is what makes its assignment a measurement rather than a choice.
grid.why_a_grid_is_admissible: the leaf carries no horizontal ruled lines (see no_horizontal_rules), so the pass before this one would commit no line number at all. But the PRINTED form is ruled at a fixed pitch whether or not the rules survived the exposure, and that pitch is measurable from the entries of columns that have nothing to do with the TOTAL column. Fitted to those 22 anchors the pitch is 75.86 px with an rms of 5.8 px — 8 per cent of a line — and every one of the 44 TOTAL-cell components then falls inside k=0..29 with none outside the range and none unassigned. A 29-consecutive-line model (no empty slot) was tested against the same anchors and is worse by a factor of three (rms 17.6, and it collapses two anchors onto one line); it is rejected.
